posts.headline: Week 11 Preview: Vitside Mafia vs Gridiron Geeks Is the Game
posts.body: The bye race runs through Vitside Mafia and Gridiron Geeks, and I'm telling you who wins it. Plus picks for all eight matchups and the NFL games that decide them.
content: Boom! Week 11 is here, and I'm told the biggest fight on the board is for a first-round bye, not a playoff spot.
Vitside Mafia and Gridiron Geeks are chasing the same prize, and this is the game that tells us who gets it. Check the live scoreboard all Sunday to see it unfold.

story: League sources tell me this is the one. Vitside Mafia (11-2) and Gridiron Geeks (10-3) are both chasing a first-round bye, and the bye odds swing hard in this game.
Vitside Mafia's bye odds are about 45 percent right now, and a win pushes that to about 79 percent. Gridiron Geeks sit around 37 percent and could jump to about 65 with a win.
The NFL game that decides it is MIA at BUF, where Josh Allen (28.8 projected) and Tyler Bass (6.6) carry Vitside Mafia's hopes. Allen is the engine of that roster and it shows.
Gridiron Geeks counter with Jordan Love (22.1) and Daniel Jones (21.2), plus Ja'Marr Chase (16.9) catching passes in Cincinnati. That is a lot of firepower.
Gridiron Geeks lead the all-time series 8-7, but Vitside Mafia took the only playoff meeting. Money is nice, but this bye is better.
My pick: Vitside Mafia, 168-149. The projections say 161 to 127, and Allen gets the edge.
Pacific Pigskins (9-4) are sitting on a three-game losing streak, and they should bounce back against Dead Cap Walking (2-11).
NO at CHI is the NFL game to watch, with Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland both on the field.
My pick: Pacific Pigskins, 131-94.
Running down the Dream (9-4) are chasing a bye at about 9 percent, and they have Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey in MIN at SF to help.
The Mariachi Ninjas have won three straight meetings, so this one is not a gimme.
My pick: Running down the Dream, 133-96.
Da Dangsters (9-4) host Midwestside Connection (6-7) in a game that barely moves the playoff needle for the favorite but matters a lot to the underdog.
My pick: Da Dangsters, 128-117.
Computer Jocks (6-7) have won the last six meetings, and Music City Mafia (2-11) has lost four straight. Bet on the streak.
My pick: Computer Jocks, 127-101.
Cowboy Up (8-5) are on a four-game win streak and sit at about 95 percent playoff odds. Dark Magicians of Chaos (5-8) have won the last four meetings, though, and Dak Prescott is a problem.
My pick: Cowboy Up, 109-104. Joe Burrow's 30.6 projected is the difference.
Wascawy Wabbits (10-3) have won three straight, and Maverick (2-11) can't stop them. Trevor Lawrence and Deshaun Watson do the heavy lifting.
My pick: Wascawy Wabbits, 150-112.
Bring The Pain (3-10) have Jahmyr Gibbs (20.6) and Emeka Egbuka (10.6) on the field in TB at DET. That is a real chance to climb out of the cellar.
My pick: Bring The Pain, 118-116.

Every add in this league costs at least the $425K league-minimum salary, so there's no such thing as a free pickup. That makes a week like this look even more deliberate, because nobody wanted to pay the price.

posts.headline: Week 10: Dangsters vs Dream Headlines a Loaded Slate
posts.body: Da Dangsters and Running down the Dream collide in the Game of the Week, Pacific Pigskins face a must-win against the Magicians, and Vitside Mafia chase a bye. Here is what to watch and who I like.
content: Boom! Week 10 is here, and the league's top two clubs are trying to keep the postseason fight from getting messy. the live scoreboard is where you'll track every one of these games as they happen.
Money is nice, but championships are better, and this week separates the contenders from the pretenders. Check the standings to see how much every win matters right now.

story: Game of the Week, and it is a big one: Da Dangsters (9-3) host Running down the Dream (8-4) in a battle of two of the best teams in the league.
Da Dangsters are riding a four-game winning streak, and a win here pushes their playoff odds to 100%, per the simulation.
Running down the Dream lead the all-time series 7-6, and they won the closest game in the rivalry's history, a 134.35-124.13 thriller back in 2019.
The swing player is QB Cam Ward, who projects 22.4 points for Running down the Dream, and TE Trey McBride, who projects 19.2 for Da Dangsters.
The key NFL game is SFO at DAL, with QB Brock Purdy and RB Christian McCaffrey on one side and WR CeeDee Lamb on the other.
My pick: Running down the Dream, 131-129, in a game that will be decided by one lineup decision late on Sunday.
Gridiron Geeks (10-2) are on a five-game winning streak and have a bye chase of their own, about 48% likely right now.
The Mariachi Ninjas (5-7) are long shots, but RB James Cook projects 16.8 for them, and the Buffalo Bills defense projects 9.1.
The key NFL game is BUF at NYJ.
My pick: Gridiron Geeks, 121-96, and the Geeks keep the bye hunt alive.
Vitside Mafia (11-1) are on a seven-game winning streak and chasing a first-round bye, which sits about 46% likely right now.
Fire Ready Aim (5-7) have lost five straight and are long shots, so this is a must-win for them only in pride.
QB Josh Allen projects 30.6 for Vitside Mafia, the biggest single number on either roster.
The key NFL game is CAR at NOS, where QB Tyler Shough of Fire Ready Aim projects 26.5 points.
My pick: Vitside Mafia, 141-118, and the bye chase keeps rolling.
Computer Jocks (6-6) have won four straight meetings with Wascawy Wabbits (9-3), even though the all-time series is dead even at 5-5.
The Jocks are on a one-game winning streak and need a win to meaningfully push their playoff odds from 15%.
QB Trevor Lawrence projects 24.5 for Wascawy Wabbits, and the key NFL game is JAC at TEN.
My pick: Wascawy Wabbits, 126-109, because the Wabbits should be too much for a Jocks team still trying to find its footing.
Pacific Pigskins (9-3) are on a two-game skid and face Dark Magicians of Chaos (4-8), who have dropped five straight.
The Pigskins need this one badly, and a win moves their playoff odds from 89% to about 95%.
QB Jared Goff projects 27.8 for Pacific Pigskins, but QB Dak Prescott (27.6) and QB Jayden Daniels (25.9) give the Magicians plenty of firepower.
My pick: Pacific Pigskins, 118-112, because Goff and the Pigskins cannot afford another slip.
Bring The Pain (2-10) are on a seven-game losing streak against Midwestside Connection (6-6), who are riding a two-game winning streak.
RB Jahmyr Gibbs projects 17.4 for Bring The Pain and is their best bet to snap the skid.
My pick: Midwestside Connection, 101-98, in a tight one.
Cowboy Up (7-5) are on a three-game winning streak and face Music City Mafia (2-10), who have won the last two meetings.
QB Joe Burrow projects 30.4 for Cowboy Up, which is the biggest number on the roster.
My pick: Cowboy Up, 101-86, and they should be fine as long as Burrow stays healthy.
Maverick (1-11) face Dead Cap Walking (2-10) in a clash of the league's bottom dwellers, and this is their first meeting under the current owners.
QB Patrick Mahomes projects 26.7 for Maverick, which gives them the edge.
My pick: Maverick, 98-84, because even a bad season needs a win sometimes.

closing: Watch SFO at DAL on Sunday for the Game of the Week swing, with QB Brock Purdy and RB Christian McCaffrey on one side and WR CeeDee Lamb on the other.

Also tune into BUF at NYJ and CAR at NOS, where QB Josh Allen and QB Tyler Shough hold the key roster spots. Check the rivalry pages to see how these matchups have played out over the years, and track it all on the live scoreboard.

posts.headline: Music City Mafia Splashes $850K on Two Waiver Adds
posts.body: Only two claims hit the wire in Week 9, and Music City Mafia made both of them count for $850K total. Every add signs at the $425K league minimum, so nothing here came free. Here's what it means and who got left out.
content: Boom! Music City Mafia was the only team moving on the wire in Week 9, and they went and grabbed two players for a combined $850K. I'm told both adds came first-come-first-served, and each one signed at the $425K league-minimum salary. Money is nice, but championships are better, and this is a team that clearly saw a need and filled it immediately. If you're scrolling the free agent board looking for the next move, you're not alone.

The headline grab is RB Audric Estime at $425K, a running back add that speaks to depth at a position where injuries and bye weeks never stop coming. The other claim was QB Carson Wentz, also at $425K, and that's a desperation-style quarterback add that tells you Music City Mafia wasn't willing to sit around hoping their starter holds up. Two players, two positions, one team making sure nobody could catch them short. That's aggressive roster management, plain and simple.

Here's the flip side: nobody else touched the wire this week, which means every other owner passed on what was available. League sources tell me a few teams are sitting on full benches and comfortable cap sheets, but staying put is still a choice, and it's one that can cost you when the next injury hits. Before you decide to sit tight again, check the rosters and see where your depth actually stands. If you want to measure how much room you really have, the salary benchmarks will show you exactly where the league's money is going.

Grade for Week 9: Music City Mafia gets an A for urgency and a B-minus for the cost, because $850K is a lot of cap to spend on two adds, even at league-minimum salaries. Everyone else gets a C for standing pat with so much available. If you're planning a move for next week, don't wait until the morning of waivers to figure out your targets. Get ahead of it on the free agent board, and you'll be the one breaking the news next time.
